subject: Redwood SDK quickstart + env setup — post-call & integration next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Kumar <amit@fintechops.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Redwood SDK quickstart + env setup — post-call recap

Hi Amit —

Great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the integration topics we covered, plus proposed next steps: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: customer support triage + enrichment pipeline (conversational reranking and contextual embeddings for agent assist).
- Volume: ~30k requests/day, 95th pct latency target ~300ms for agent-facing flows.
- Security: data residency and SOC2 evidence needed; prefer VPC/private when going to production.

Integration/architecture notes we discussed:
- SDKs: Python + TypeScript quickstart are the fastest path to a PoC.
- Auth: API key for PoC, KMS-backed tokens for production; we support short-lived tokens and token rotation via our Private offering.
- Routing: can route user-facing traffic to low-latency hosted models and background batch reranks to Dedicated capacity.
- Structured output & tool calling: SDK supports function/tool-calling payloads and schema validation (we showed the order-enrichment example).
- Embeddings & rerankers: we recommend using Redwood embeddings with an initial 1536-d vector for semantic matching; re-ranker model can be a light-weight candidate scorer hosted on Dedicated.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll share a SDK quickstart bundle you can run locally (Python + TS sample apps).
2) Devs spin up the local quickstart and try the example: chat -> embedding -> rerank flow. We’ll be available for a 30-min pairing session.
3) You share the security questionnaire (or we can have your security team send it to security@redwood.ai).
4) If PoC looks good, we’ll scope capacity and a Dedicated pilot.

Attachments: Redwood SDK quickstart (zip), integration guide (pdf), architecture diagram (png).

Let me know which day/time works for the pairing session this week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Amit — answers inline below, and I attached the quickstart bundle:

1) Auth for PoC:
- You can use a long-lived API key for the fastest path; however, the SDK supports exchanging GCP service-account JWTs for short-lived Redwood tokens via our token endpoint. Devs often use API keys locally and switch to token-exchange (service account) in CI/prod. We included example scripts in the quickstart under /auth.

2) Embeddings -> vector store:
- The quickstart includes an example that writes embeddings to a local FAISS index (Python) and a TypeScript example that shows integration points for Pinecone/Chromadb (comments point to the exact files). See /samples/embeddings_faiss.py and /samples/ts/embeddings-chroma.md.

3) Reranker model for CPU:
- For low-latency CPU scoring we recommend a distilled cross-encoder like miniLM-based reranker (we include a placeholder candidate-scorer in the quickstart that uses a small transformer; see /samples/reranker_cpu.py). For better latency/throughput you can move the reranker to our Dedicated pool.

Pairing session: Thursday 8/13 10:00am PT works for our team — adding a calendar invite now.

Quickstart notes (run locally):
- Python: python3.9+, venv recommended; pip install -r requirements.txt; export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx; python samples/run_local_chat.py
- TypeScript: Node 18+, npm install; copy .env.example -> .env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY; npm run dev (local sample at http://localhost:3000)
- Local test data: /samples/test_prompts.json included for regression checks.

If your devs run into env issues I’ll jump on the pairing session and we can walk through the logs.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Amit — quick operational notes from our infra/dev side before the pairing session: 

- Service account token exchange:
  * We have a sample script in quickstart /auth/exchange_gcp_jwt.sh that demonstrates exchanging a signed JWT for a short-lived Redwood token. For the PoC you can run it locally using gcloud to create a signed JWT.
- Local troubleshooting checklist (if the TS sample doesn't load):
  1) Ensure Node version >=18 (we recommend using nvm).
  2) Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_TOKEN in .env. The quickstart checks both.
  3) If embeddings are returning identical vectors, check that you installed faiss-cpu in the Python venv (notes in requirements.txt).
- Security/SOC2: Marissa — I attached the integration guide which includes the SOC2 evidence checklist; Amit — if you share your questionnaire we’ll map items to artifacts and provide timelines.

See you on the call at 10am PT.

Cheers,
